bib.title: SUPER-NATURALINSTRUCTIONS: Generalization via Declarative Instructions on 1600+ NLP Tasks
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 5085-5109

read.skipped: Appendix G/H per-task tables and task example tables 6-17 skimmed (lists of task ids, examples); references skimmed.

question: How well can NLP models generalize to unseen tasks when given only in-context task instructions, when trained on a large collection of tasks with instructions?
hypothesis: Training on a large, diverse set of tasks with declarative instructions lets a smaller model follow instructions on unseen tasks better than much larger instruction-tuned models.
contributions: SUP-NATINST, a benchmark of 1,616 NLP tasks with expert-written instructions across 76 task types
Tk-Instruct and mTk-Instruct, T5/mT5 models trained to follow in-context instructions
Analysis of generalization versus number of tasks, instances per task, model size and instruction elements

method.summary: A community-built meta-dataset of 1,616 tasks, each with a definition and positive/negative examples, is split into 757 English training tasks and 154 held-out evaluation tasks (119 English, 35 cross-lingual). T5-11B and mT5-13B are fine-tuned on instruction+input encodings and scored with ROUGE-L in open-ended generation against heuristics, T5-LM, GPT-3, T0, InstructGPT and a supervised upper bound.

datasets.name: SUP-NATINST
datasets.size: 1616 tasks, ~5M instances, avg 3106.0 instances per task, 76 task types, 55 languages, 33 domains, 576 non-English tasks; instances capped at 6.5K per task
datasets.split: eval: 12 manually selected categories = 154 tasks (119 English, 35 cross-lingual), max 100 instances per task = 15,310 test instances; train: 757 tasks (English track) or 1271 tasks (cross-lingual track), after excluding tasks from the same source dataset as any test task
datasets.source: 88 contributors via GitHub (github.com/allenai/natural-instructions); public datasets, crowdsourcing intermediate annotations, synthetic tasks
datasets.preprocessing: Automatic checks, 1-2 peer reviewers (4-6 iterations), 3 AMT workers per English task give feedback; avg 2.8 positive and 2.4 negative examples, 56.6-word definitions

models.name: Tk-Instruct
models.params: 11B (3B for analyses; small/base/large/xl/xxl for size study)
models.init_from: T5.1.1.xxl checkpoint (C4 only); T5-LM checkpoint tried and was worse

models.name: Supervised upper bound
models.params: T5-11B (119 English tasks); mT5-13B (35 non-English tasks)
models.architecture: fine-tuned on 1K random training instances per evaluation task

training.objective: inferred: supervised seq2seq (text-to-text) fine-tuning on enc(instruction, input) -> output; loss not named
training.lr: 1e-5 constant (both T5-11B TPU and smaller GPU runs)
training.hardware: T5-11B: Google V3-256 TPUs; smaller models: 8 A100 GPUs with 48GB each, DeepSpeed
training.wall_clock: T5-11B: 4 hours per run; smaller models: 6 hours per run

other.default_instruction_encoding: task definition + 2 positive examples, no negatives or explanations
other.instances_per_task_in_training: not stated for main model; Fig 5b varies it, saturating at 64

inference.decoding: GPT-3/InstructGPT via OpenAI API: temperature 0; local models decoding not stated
inference.samples: GPT-3 and InstructGPT: 20 random instances from each of 119 English test tasks; others: max 100 instances per task; single run
inference.prompting: Same encoding for all methods: definition + 2 positive examples (Fig 8 template) then 'Now complete the following example- input: ... output:'

other.api_date: All API requests were made on May 30, 2022

metrics.name: ROUGE-L
metrics.definition: soft string overlap, aggregated over tasks; open-ended generation, no option ranking

metrics.name: Exact Match
metrics.definition: used per task for classification-style categories in Table 5

metrics.name: Human preference
metrics.definition: fraction of instances where model output rated at least as good as ground truth (tie allowed), AMT, 60 tasks x 10 instances, English only

eval.protocol: Single run, no seeds or significance tests stated. Analyses on English track with T5-3B. Human eval: crowdworkers from US/UK/Canada/Australia, 5000+ HITs, >=99% approval.

results.quote: an 11B-parameter Tk-INSTRUCT can out- perform the 175B-parameter InstructGPT model by 9.9 ROUGE-L points when evaluated on 119 unseen English tasks

limits: Skewed to English, short responses; task-type distribution skewed (Appendix F)
ROUGE-L is a weak proxy for rewriting and error-correction tasks where copying input scores high
InstructGPT training data may overlap with evaluation tasks since it is unavailable
Largest models not trained due to compute budget
Analyses use T5-3B on English track only; single run, no seeds or significance tests stated
InstructGPT/GPT-3 evaluated on only 20 instances per task, text-davinci-001 (May 2022)
Explanations hurt only for models of this size, per authors
